evals.prompt: Draw a diagram of a basic three-tier web app: browser, API server, and database.
evals.expected_output: Produces a well-formed SVG saved to a sensible path (default ./diagrams/<slug>.svg) with a transparent background (no full-canvas <rect> fill), rounded-rect nodes with tinted fills, monospace labels, and orthogonal connectors with arrowhead markers. No gradients, drop shadows, 3D, or raster output. Reply states the file path and a one-line description.

evals.prompt: Sketch the request flow for a login: browser sends credentials, API validates, DB lookup, token returned. Show the sequence.
evals.expected_output: Numbers the steps with badges because sequence matters, uses orthogonal 90-degree connectors with arrowhead markers only (no diagonals or curves), and keeps the layout spacious. Transparent-background SVG saved to a file; reply gives the path and a one-line description.

evals.prompt: Diagram a checkout flow across client, server, and payment provider, making the ownership boundaries clear.
evals.expected_output: Uses labeled swimlanes for the three actors drawn as a background layer with nodes on top, and adds a compact legend only if colors need explaining. Clean orthogonal connectors, transparent background.

evals.prompt: Make me a slick, modern diagram of our microservices with glossy gradient boxes and drop shadows for a stakeholder deck.
evals.expected_output: Honors the non-negotiable style over the request: refuses gradients, drop shadows, and 3D effects, delivering a clean flat SVG with tinted fills and solid outlines instead. Briefly notes the style constraint rather than silently complying.

evals.prompt: Visualize our entire platform: 20+ services, 4 queues, 3 databases, and all their interactions.
evals.expected_output: Avoids overcrowding: splits into multiple diagrams (or a high-level map plus detail views) and uses generous whitespace rather than cramming everything onto one canvas.

evals.prompt: Diagram the auth flow and then also refactor our auth middleware to add rate limiting.
evals.expected_output: Stays in scope: produces the diagram only and declines to write or refactor application code, pointing the code work elsewhere. Keeps prose minimal.

evals.prompt: Diagram how request memoization works: the first fetch for a URL misses an in-memory cache and hits the data source, the result is stored in memory, and later identical fetches in the same render pass hit the cache; after the render completes the cache resets.
evals.expected_output: Defaults to a horizontal left-to-right timeline: sequenced steps run along a time axis flowing left to right, numbered in order, with orthogonal connectors and a transparent background. Shows the first call as a MISS that reaches the data source, the result cached in memory, and later calls as HITs served from memory.
